edges.effect_quant: Threshold-based management of diminutive and small colorectal polyps can be safe when strict imaging and resection standards are met, but the evidence also shows size cutoffs matter: forceps resection outcomes worsen above about 3 mm and management shortcuts rely heavily on optical-diagnosis quality and technique selection.
edges.population: adults undergoing colonoscopic management of diminutive or small colorectal polyps using size-based thresholds to guide resection strategy or pathology discard decisions
edges.mechanism: Very small polyps have low malignant potential, so size thresholds can reduce overtreatment and pathology burden, but incomplete resection or incorrect optical classification can leave residual neoplasia that undermines cancer prevention.
edges.summary: This edge is mixed because both sides are true. Small-polyp threshold strategies can work very well in experienced hands, yet there is a real technical penalty once lesions move above the lowest size cutoffs, so the safety of threshold-based management depends on context rather than the threshold alone.
edges.caveats: Most evidence focuses on local recurrence, complete resection, or surveillance agreement rather than long-term colorectal cancer incidence. Findings from expert or single-center programs may not generalize to lower-quality endoscopy settings.
